title: The Admin area's own username and password on a machine without accounts, and a lockout on every password sign-in
request: The owner asked for an admin-only section, behind only a username and a password, for the owner alone.
spec: Once an admin login is set in the workspace folder, the owner-only permissions (admin, timelines) need its session; everything else stays as it is; with no login set nothing changes. The password is a hash, the session a hashed token in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie that ends when idle or old; wrong passwords lock the sign-in; every sign-in, failure, lock, sign-out and change is audited without the password.
plan: the login, session and lockout module with its tests
the guard: a locked local owner is refused the owner-only permissions
the sign-in routes and the command line admin-set
the sign-in card on the Admin page
the same lockout on the account sign-in

decisions.decision: A separate admin login in the workspace folder, not the accounts system
decisions.why: the owner chose to keep local work as it is; the accounts need PostgreSQL and change every page

decisions.decision: With no admin login file nothing changes
decisions.why: the tests, a clean checkout and the command line keep working as the local owner

decisions.decision: The login is created only from the command line
decisions.why: nothing in a browser can create the first admin on an open machine

decisions.decision: The lockout counts by login, not by address
decisions.why: locally every request comes from this machine, so an address count would mean nothing

change: dclab_rnd/accounts/admin_login.py and admin_api.py (new); accounts/principal.py (admin_locked); accounts/guard.py (PUBLIC sign-in routes, ADMIN_ONLY, identify, demand); accounts/__main__.py (admin-set, admin-remove); accounts/api.py (lockout of the account sign-in); audit.py (kind admin); agentic/server.py (the router); views/admin.html and look.css (the sign-in card), the generated app; CLAUDE.md; tests/test_admin_login.py.

findings.defect: The account sign-in had no limit on wrong passwords
findings.scenario: with DCLAB_AUTH=password a guesser could try passwords without end; only a short sleep slowed each one
findings.fix: five wrong passwords for one login within fifteen minutes lock it for fifteen minutes

findings.defect: On a machine without accounts every page and every owner-only route was open to anyone at the browser
findings.scenario: another person at the Mac, or another browser tab, could open the Admin page, the session records and the routing switches
findings.cause: without DCLAB_AUTH every request was the owner
findings.fix: an admin login set from the command line makes the owner-only permissions need its session

findings.defect: A burst of guesses skipped the account lockout
findings.scenario: many password guesses for one login sent at once all passed the lock check before the first failure was counted, and a right one inside the burst was accepted
findings.cause: the attempt was counted only after its password was checked
findings.fix: each attempt is counted before its password is checked; the attempt that reaches the limit is refused unchecked

findings.defect: The failure table could grow without end
findings.scenario: wrong passwords for ever new login strings each added an entry that was never removed
findings.cause: the table was keyed by what callers send and pruned only on a lock or a success
findings.fix: logins are cut to a fixed length and the table is pruned and capped

findings.defect: The routing switches and the audit trail stayed open without the admin session
findings.scenario: another person at the machine could switch a model's tier or read the audit while the Admin area was locked
findings.cause: the gate covered the admin and timelines permissions only; these need review or read
findings.fix: review and a new audit permission are guarded too on a machine without accounts; with accounts every member still reads the audit

findings.defect: The admin username was given to anyone before sign-in
findings.scenario: the public me route returned the username, half of the credential
findings.cause: state returned it whether signed in or not

findings.defect: A leftover admin login asked for a second sign-in on a server with accounts, and could be locked by strangers
findings.scenario: with DCLAB_AUTH set the page showed the card and the public sign-in route counted failures
findings.cause: the admin routes did not know accounts were on
findings.fix: with accounts on, me says nothing is required and sign-in answers not found

findings.defect: A hand-edited session file could make every request fail
findings.scenario: a time without a time zone in the session file raised inside identify, which runs on every request
findings.cause: the comparison sat outside the guard that skips a broken entry
findings.fix: a broken entry is no session

findings.defect: The lockout test read the audit from a file that does not exist on PostgreSQL
findings.scenario: the nightly full gate's PostgreSQL pass: the audit was written to the database and the test opened audit.jsonl
findings.cause: the test assumed the file audit
findings.fix: the test reads the audit through the server's own audit log, files or PostgreSQL

measurements.name: the sign-in in the browser
measurements.gate: the flow by hand on the preview server
measurements.result: the card hides the Admin tabs; a wrong password is refused; the right one opens them; sign-out locks them again and the benchmark route refuses; the audit keeps the sign-ins and no password
limits: one browser on this machine; the lockout of the account sign-in is kept in one server process and a restart forgets it

outcome: The owner can lock the Admin area with a username and password of their own; the rest of DCLab works as before.
lessons: a protection that only hides a page is not one: the routes behind it must refuse too, and a test must call them
a lock counted after the check it guards lets a burst through: count first, then check
risks: it does not protect against someone who can read the workspace folder or the database
the account lockout is per process, not shared between server processes
